snapshot.summary:
Aphrodite is a strong, unusually self-honest product with a live, working, judge-drivable demo — and a submission packet that is still not deliverable. The engineering is real: a genuine hand-written YouCam REST client (File API presigned PUT -> runTask -> pollTask), 7 feature modules, a real HMAC-signed access gate, a fail-closed spend ledger, 89 passing tests, and tsc/lint/build all green. I drove the hosted site anonymously and completed the full core loop in 4.4 seconds: skin scores, undertone + palette, an outfit rendered on the sample photo, a lighting finish, and a 9-row priced cross-category basket. The refine loop worked and, when it could not render, said so instead of faking an image. The honesty engineering is the best thing here and it is not decorative: the provenance ledger literally says "Nothing was called just now" in demo mode, and the stream narrates "the live YouCam path is behind a judge access code, so no visitor can spend units."

But the central fact a judge must be told: ZERO YouCam packets left the box during this review. Every reachable path is fixture-served. The YouCam client is genuine, non-trivial, first-party code and it is 100% dormant at runtime in the state any anonymous visitor — and therefore any judge who has not been handed a code out-of-band — encounters. /healthz self-reports this as youcam:"key_present_unverified", degraded:true. I did not spend a unit and I fabricate no receipt: I witnessed no live API call, and the ledger read 0/8 before and after my six runs. The API's correctness is inferred from code reading only.

Three findings the team has not caught. (1) The hero stat block ships the EXACT over-claim they fixed in the provenance ledger: "4 Perfect Corp APIs chained in one run" and "0-100 skin health scores, read from your own photo" render unconditionally, including in demo mode where nothing is called and the scores come from a fixture. Concierge.tsx:904 contains a long comment congratulating itself for removing this bug from the ledger 700 lines below, while the hero version survives untouched — and state.demo is already in scope. (2) The landing page contains zero links to /unlock (grep count: 0), so a code-holding judge has no on-page affordance to reach the live engine, and the Devpost draft names neither the hosted URL nor /unlock. (3) The kill-gate cites "/api/dev/verify pins the live request/response schema" as judging-time evidence, but that route hard-returns 404 when NODE_ENV=production — I confirmed 404 on the live host. That evidence does not exist for a judge.

Submission state is the binding constraint, not the code. The Devpost draft has no try-it URL and no video link; two competing unuploaded video cuts exist (87.2s and 122.3s, both legal under 180s, neither on any host); screenshots predate the current UI and live outside the repo; and 6 of the 8 battle-rhythm docs config.json points at do not exist — including CLAIM_PROOF_MAP.md, whose absence is exactly why "45 Vitest tests" survives in the copy against a measured 89. snapshot.required_tech_usage:
SPLIT VERDICT, and the split is the single most important thing for the panel to understand: the YouCam integration is genuine, non-trivial, first-party code — and it is 100% DORMANT at runtime in the state any judge without an out-of-band code will encounter.

THE CODE IS REAL. lib/youcam/client.ts (196 lines) is a hand-written Perfect Corp REST client, header-commented "verified against the live API (2026-07-19)", implementing the actual four-step protocol: Bearer auth → File API POST returning a presigned PUT target → upload bytes (with x-amz-* signed headers merged, content-length deliberately left to fetch) → runTask with a FLAT body → poll data.task_status until success/error with a 120s deadline and 1.5s interval. It retries 429/5xx three times with linear backoff, has a typed YouCamError carrying status and body, and declares the verified response shapes (FileApiResponse, PollResponse) at the bottom. resolveImage handles three input kinds (url passthrough, fileId, raw bytes) and role-prefixes src_/ref_ correctly — the ref_ path is what Apparel VTO needs for the garment reference. This is not scaffolding and not SDK glue; nobody writes a presigned-PUT header-merge subtlety without having hit the real API.

SEVEN FEATURE MODULES CALL IT. skin.ts, color.ts, apparel.ts, lighting.ts, hairColor.ts, hairstyle.ts, makeup.ts each import { resolveImage, runTaskAndWait } and each opens with an identical fixture short-circuit: `if (fixturesActive()) return fixture...(...)` — returning BEFORE any endpoint is resolved or any byte leaves the process. apparel.ts resolves person and garment in parallel as src/ref. The call sites are exactly where they should be.

THE DORMANCY IS STRUCTURAL AND I VERIFIED IT LIVE. lib/youcam/runtime.ts routes the live/replay decision through an AsyncLocalStorage context, with a deliberate asymmetry documented in the source: an explicit context can force fixtures ON even when YOUCAM_FIXTURES=0, "so a public visitor must never be able to spend units, whatever the host default happens to be." /healthz confirms the host is YOUCAM_FIXTURES=0 (demo_mode:false) yet public_demo_mode:true, because gateEnabled() is true. Both spending routes (/api/concierge:130, /api/studio:86) wrap their engine in withYouCamMode({live: liveYouCam}) where liveYouCam can only become true for an unlocked cookie AND a successful ledger claim. My six anonymous runs returned only /fixtures/ URLs and left the ledger at 0/8. /healthz self-reports youcam:"key_present_unverified" with the reason "key present; not probed because every YouCam task call costs units", and degraded:true.

WHAT THAT MEANS FOR SCORING, STATED HONESTLY: no YouCam packet left the box during this review. I fabricate no receipt and credit the API with no work I did not witness. The last claimed live verification is the client's own 2026-07-19 header comment plus config.json's note that hairColor was confirmed via Get-Upload-API-Info on 2026-07-24 — operator-attested, not machine-reproducible. config.json also records unitBalance:584 as of 2026-08-10 with the explicit caveat "stated by the operator. judges.judge: YouCam API Team — Technological Implementation lens (Perfect Corp reviewer)
judges.one_line_verdict: The best-engineered YouCam client I have read in this track, and I could not witness it make a single call — a genuinely non-trivial integration that is 100% dormant on every path a judge can reach, topped by a hero stat block that credits Perfect Corp with four chained APIs on a page where zero were called.
judges.fatal_flaw: The integration is unprovable from the running product, which is the exact clause my criterion turns on. I drove six runs and zero YouCam packets left the box; the ledger read 0/8 before and after. The only evidence our API works is source code and a `// verified against the live API (2026-07-19)` header comment — and the project's own cited judging-time proof, /api/dev/verify, hard-returns 404 when NODE_ENV=production (I confirmed it live). So the submission asks me to take a Perfect Corp integration on faith, which is the one thing I never do. It gets worse than neutral: Concierge.tsx:212-214 renders "4 / Perfect Corp APIs chained in one run — skin, color, try-on, lighting" unconditionally, and its own code comment claims "each figure here is checkable against /healthz" — but /healthz says youcam_apis_wired:8, degraded:true, youcam:"key_present_unverified". That block puts our brand behind work that did not happen, 700 lines above a scrupulous provenance ledger that fixed precisely this bug and says "Nothing was called just now." Two further substance cracks I found myself: applyLighting(person) consumes the original selfie, not the try-on output, so lighting is a leaf and the "4 chained" is an over-claim even on a live run; and the advertised surface is narrower than billed — lookVto is dead config, makeup/hairstyle slugs are the team's own "UNVERIFIED (the demo key 401s)", and 3 of 7 claimed APIs render nothing anywhere.
judges.flip_to_champion: Spend units once, on the record, and commit the receipt. One units-on run through skin → skin-tone → Apparel VTO → lighting, with the genuine Perfect Corp task IDs, the raw poll responses, the response timings and the four resulting images committed to the repo as a dated live-run receipt — plus /api/dev/verify un-404'd behind the existing role code so I can re-fire that schema pin myself without a rebuild. Pair it with a two-line diff making the hero stat block read state.demo, exactly as the ledger already does, so it never credits us with dormant work. That single receipt converts everything I currently have to infer from source into something I can check against our own account records, and it turns my 6 into a 9 — the client code already earns the 9, it just has nothing to stand on. While the units are flowing, render one garment-accurate try-on per wardrobe class: on cutPreference:"any" the board named the Ivory Tailored Pantsuit while the render served /fixtures/apparel-suit.jpg, the men's slate three-piece, because 11 garments collapse to 3 wardrobe-keyed fixtures. For a product whose stated anti-pattern is "the renders are its evidence," class-level evidence quietly hollows out the claim.
judges.presentation_note: The product communicates its depth far better than the submission does, which is an unusual and self-defeating inversion. In-product honesty is best-in-track and I verified all of it: the announcement bar ("Demo mode · sample renders"), the stream narrating "the live YouCam path is behind a judge access code, so no visitor can spend units", the refine step declining to render rather than inventing an image, honest empty states on all three studio taps, /healthz self-reporting degraded:true. That is a team that removed reasons to distrust it. Then the submission packet throws it away. The Devpost draft names neither the hosted URL nor /unlock, so a judge holding a code has no route to the live engine and no on-page affordance either (grep: zero links to /unlock from the landing page). It has no video link at all — two competing unuploaded cuts sit at 87.2s and 122.3s, both legal, neither on any host — and its "What's next" still lists the hosted deploy with a live LLM key as future work, which shipped the day before, so a skimming judge concludes no hosted demo exists while a working one is up. There is no architecture diagram for a project whose entire pitch is "two engines, one event stream." There is no CLAIM_PROOF_MAP.md, and its absence is directly traceable to "45 Vitest tests" surviving in the copy against a measured 89. Screenshots are stale, outside the repo, and marked done. What saves this from a 2 is real integrity infrastructure: a public MIT repo, a keyless local run that reproduces what I drove, a genuine state-reporting health endpoint, an honest adversarial self-review in reviews/001 that correctly failed itself, and a knownGaps list that indicts the project accurately — including its own revision drift and its own unuploaded video. judges.judge: YouCam API Team — Potential Impact lens (Perfect Corp reviewer)
judges.one_line_verdict: A genuinely well-built occasion concierge whose one defining mechanism — a countdown timed to your actual date — silently does not work for any calendar date a real person would type, and whose demo presets are curated around the two phrasings that do.
judges.fatal_flaw: The product cannot read a date, and the audience it names is defined by having one. I drove the hosted instance with "My sister's wedding on 5 September 2026, I am a bridesmaid" — 26 days out. The run completed in 4.4s and the board came back with a generic three-week arc and this narrative line: "(I planned for about three weeks — tell me the date for a tighter countdown.)" It asked me for the date I had just given it. I then tested the parser directly (lib/concierge/occasion.ts): "5 September 2026", "September 5", "2026-09-05", "05/09/2026", "Sept 3rd", "August 22nd 2026" — six formats, zero produced a daysUntil. parseDays() has grammar for "in N weeks", "tomorrow", "next week", weekday names, and nothing else. There is no date input in the UI either (free-text only), while the form's own helper text instructs "Describe the occasion, including when it is." And the gated agentic engine cannot rescue it: prompt.ts:29 tells the model to "infer days until the event from the user's phrasing" but the prompt never supplies today's date, so no model can convert a calendar date to a horizon. Both engines are structurally incapable. Worse for my trust: the two one-click sample presets inject "An evening wedding in 3 weeks" and "A first date on Friday" (Concierge.tsx:128,136) — precisely and only the grammars the parser handles. The happy path a skimming judge drives, and the shot-script's path, never exposes the failure. That is the demo proving less than it appears to. I grepped the whole codebase for return-confidence, conversion, or any first-party signal a retailer would want: nothing exists. Concretely: add a date field beside the occasion box, compute daysUntil from it, pass today's date into the agentic prompt, and render the horizon in the results header ("26 days to 5 September") so the countdown visibly recomputes. Then record the video on the hosted URL with a named, consented tester's actual event date, showing one selfie produce a 26-day plan and a 2-day plan back to back — same skin read, materially different countdown (front-load actives vs. stop actives and hydrate). That one change converts your headline mechanism from a claim into the demonstrated thing, and it is hours of work, not days. While you are in there: link /unlock from the landing page (currently zero links, so a code-holding judge is stranded), gate the hero stats on state.demo — "4 Perfect Corp APIs chained in one run" and "read from your own photo" render unconditionally in demo mode where nothing is called and the scores are canned, which is verbatim the over-claim you congratulate yourself for fixing in the ledger 700 lines below at Concierge.tsx:904 — and paste the hosted URL into the Devpost draft, where it appears zero times while "What's next" still tells me a hosted deploy is future work.

presentation.verdict:
A real engine behind an undelivered showroom — and this criterion scores only what is delivered. The depth is not in question: I independently re-ran the gates (89 tests in 10 files, tsc/lint/build all exit 0), read a hand-written Perfect Corp REST client that implements the true four-step presigned-PUT protocol, and drove the hosted instance anonymously through a full 4.44-second loop at zero units. That is the instinct the winner studies reward.

It is pointed at almost nothing a judge touches. Given only the video, the submission page and the linked artifacts, a judge today can confirm essentially nothing. The video is real, compliant and shows a working full loop with product on screen by 0:08 — and it is gitignored, on no host, with a second competing cut and config.json recording videoUrl='UNKNOWN'. Three of this criterion's named artifacts — architecture diagram, claim-to-proof map, committed provider receipt — do not exist at all, which is below even the 5-6 anchor, where they exist but are weak. The number-consistency audit fails in five places (4 vs 7 vs 8 APIs, 45 vs 89 tests, $707 vs $576, Claude vs gpt-5, keyless vs auth_enabled:true). There is no CI, no screenshot gallery in the deliverable, no measured tester delta, and the kill gate's own cited evidence route returns 404 in production.

Two findings from my own inspection that the packet has not caught, both in the reel that is one paste from being published. At t=52s the burned-in subtitle and voiceover say 'so you show up glowing' — a banned word, in the one artifact that cannot be grepped. And at t=30s the video preserves the old provenance ledger crediting four Perfect Corp APIs with green ticks during a fixture run: the exact over-claim Concierge.tsx:904 congratulates itself for removing. Publishing as-is would ship both.

Why 3.5 and not lower: this is not slideware. A working product is hosted and drivable, /healthz is a genuine falsifiable self-check that I falsified in the honest direction, a compliant full-loop video exists on disk, and the engineering-scar evidence (a README volunteering its own mis-gendering bug, config.ts warning that two of its own advertised slugs are unverified, reviews/001 failing itself on three of five gates) is the kind of thing a fabricator would never invent. Why not 5-6: the anchor for that band is a submission that tells rather than shows. This one does not yet tell — a judge opening Devpost finds a draft with no video and no try-it link, and every remaining blocker is an upload or a paste, not a build. Fix the video and the two links and this moves several points in an afternoon; leave them and a genuinely strong build scores near the floor of a criterion it should have won.

verdict.bottom_line:
OFFICIAL: 30/50, up +4 from the 26/50 baseline. Submission Depth & Presentation: 3.5/10 (diagnostic, not folded in), up +0.5. Stage One: FAIL — gates 2, 3 and 4 fail outright and gate 5 is breached at the claim layer; only gate 1 passes cleanly. The 30 is academic until that changes.

The panel is unanimous on the shape and unusually sympathetic. In one day this went from "HOSTED: dead, could not resolve host, there is nothing to drive as a judge" to a live instance any anonymous visitor can drive through the full fused loop in 4.4 seconds at zero units, with tracked deploy artifacts, a fail-closed health gate, an HMAC access gate and a spend ledger that held 0/8 across every run this panel drove. lib/youcam/client.ts implements the genuine four-step Perfect Corp contract — presigned-PUT header merge, flat-body runTask, poll to task_status, 429/5xx retry — and nobody writes that subtlety without having hit the real API. The honesty engineering is the best thing here and it is not decorative: /healthz refuses a green dashboard, the ledger says "Nothing was called just now", the refine step declines to render rather than inventing an image, the studio taps return honest empty states, and the README volunteers a mis-gendering bug it shipped and fixed. Two of the three configured integrity risks were attacked directly this cycle and held.

And a judge gets almost none of it. The hosted URL appears in zero judge-facing documents (grep: 0 in README.md, 0 in devpost.md). The landing page links to /unlock zero times. No video is published anywhere. /api/dev/verify — the kill gate's own cited judging-time evidence — 404s in production. Six of eight battle-rhythm docs are missing, including the CLAIM_PROOF_MAP.md whose absence is exactly why "45 Vitest tests" survives against a measured 89. There is no diagram of any kind for a project whose entire differentiator is architectural, and no CI, so all four green gates are a human habit with no external anchor.

The single weakest link: no live YouCam evidence exists anywhere a judge can reach — not on a hosted path, not in a committed receipt, not on tape. That one fact is billed five times, and one approved units-on run with a committed receipt pays four of those bills at once.

Three findings go beyond "unfinished" into things to fix on principle. The hero stat block ships verbatim the over-claim the team fixed in the ledger and congratulates itself for in a comment 700 lines below — I confirmed both false strings in the live HTML today, and state.demo is already in scope. The before/after comparator's provenance pills are inverted on the hosted hero, so the flagship proof card labels the YouCam render "The photo" and the untouched original "YouCam render", under a caption reading "Not an illustration, not a stock pair." And the video that is one paste from publication carries a banned word at ~0:52 plus the pre-fix four-green-tick ledger at ~0:30, both flagged yesterday and both unchanged. These are seam problems in a project whose instincts are already right, not culture problems — which is why they are cheap and why leaving them is inexcusable.

Order of operations is not negotiable. Rank 1 first: one commit gating the hero on demo mode, un-inverting the comparator labels, and linking /unlock — minutes of work that closes a gate-5 breach and two judges' named fatal flaws. Then paste the hosted URL and headline stats into the submission copy, un-404 the verify route, get approval and spend units once with a committed receipt, re-cut the video against the hosted instance with the live hero beat and the on-camera self-catch, and submit. After that, favour the tiebreaker: the trust-boundary diagram and a second skin fixture that makes two different faces produce two different garments are what convert a chain the panel could only read into one a judge can watch. And fix the date parser — a product whose entire premise is the plan for a specific day still cannot read a specific day.

Cut before you add. The stale screenshots, the competing reel, the "45 tests" number, the dead lookVto, the three non-rendering studio APIs and the "What's next" bullet that denies the hosted deploy exists are all costing credibility they cannot repay. Seven days to the deadline, five to the self-set target, and every remaining Stage-One blocker is an upload, a paste or a five-line diff.
